subject: DPA redline: telemetry opt-out + SummitMetrics subprocessor exception
messages:
From: Claire Zhang <claire@clearwavehealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@clearwavehealth.com
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA redline: telemetry opt-out & subprocessor ask

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our proposed DPA redline (ClearWave_DPA_Redline_v3.docx) — three asks in particular we need to resolve before the pilot:

1) Telemetry opt-out: we need language that allows our customers to opt out of telemetry/analytics collection for their workspace by default.
2) Subprocessor: SummitMetrics is a 3rd-party analytics vendor Redwood uses. ClearWave cannot have SummitMetrics process telemetry related to our protected health flows; we need them removed as a subprocessor or an explicit exception limited to a 30-day pilot scope.
3) No training: we need an explicit clause that customer data will not be used to train models or be included in downstream training datasets.

For the pilot we could accept a narrow exception that keeps SummitMetrics as an analytics subprocessor if they provide SOC 2 Type II evidence, sign a subprocessor addendum that prohibits model training and limits retention to 30 days, and agrees to no cross-customer joins on PII.

Can you route this to product/security and let us know what’s feasible (and how long sign-off will take)? We’re aiming to kick the pilot the week of Nov 15.

Attachment: ClearWave_DPA_Redline_v3.docx (docx, 82KB)

Regards,
Claire Zhang
Head of Partnerships
ClearWave Health

Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline: telemetry opt-out & subprocessor ask

Thanks for the summary, Aisha. Quick security read: the proposed path is plausible but comes with conditions. High-level stance: we can consider a scoped exception for the pilot if SummitMetrics demonstrates the following and we codify controls in a subprocessor addendum: 

- Evidence: latest SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent) + completed security questionnaire (they uploaded a doc but we need the report).
- No model training: explicit contractual clause preventing use of customer data for model training or derivation; we should define "training" and prohibit any offline model builds from exported telemetry.
- Data minimization & retention: retention capped at 30 days for telemetry coming from ClearWave, documented in the addendum.
- Access controls: support for customer-scoped keys / dedicated tenant separation for telemetry when possible.
- Audit hooks: SummitMetrics must agree to produce access logs on request for the pilot and allow a short security review.

Open technical risks: SummitMetrics integrates via an event stream that currently includes some request metadata we consider high-cardinality. Product would need to add filters before forwarding. Also, we need to ensure telemetry opt-out does not break health-critical alerting flows—product to confirm what’s safe to turn off.

Ben/Laura: please draft protected-language for the addendum (no-training, 30d retention, access logs). I can review the technical controls. If SummitMetrics can provide SOC2 + signed addendum within 5 business days, we can approve a 30-day pilot exception; otherwise decline.

Olga Petrov
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment referenced: SummitMetrics_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (pdf, 128KB)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline: telemetry opt-out & subprocessor ask

Product notes on feasibility and impact:

- Telemetry opt-out: we can ship a per-customer telemetry opt-out flag scoped to analytics events within ~2 sprints (rough estimate: 3 devs, 2 sprints to build flag + gating + e2e tests). We should implement it as a policy at ingestion so we never forward excluded events to downstream processors.
- SummitMetrics exclusion: we can add a routing rule to prevent forwarding events from specific accounts to specific subprocessors. That will add ~1 sprint to the effort to add config and safe-fail behavior.
- Non-breaking: we need to enumerate which telemetry events are required for safety/alerting. If ClearWave opts out of all telemetry, we must provide an alternative for critical health signals (webhook or dedicated alerting channel) — otherwise we risk missing alerting during the pilot. Suggest a list of "required events" that cannot be turned off; require PO sign-off from ClearWave on that list.

Operational suggestion: allow a "pilot mode" toggle: opt-out for analytics but continue required alerting events. Product can expose the toggle in Console and mark the account as "pilot-exception" so downstream routing is deterministic.

Estimate: end-to-end (addendum signed + dev + security review) ~3 weeks if SummitMetrics provides SOC2 immediately. Longer if we need legal negotiation.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Product Management, Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: DPA redline: telemetry opt-out & subprocessor ask

Claire — thanks for the clearest ask. Internal alignment update and next steps: 

1) Security (Olga) and Product (Grace) are willing to support a time-boxed pilot exception provided SummitMetrics supplies SOC 2 Type II evidence and signs a narrow subprocessor addendum that contains: explicit no-training language, retention capped at 30 days for ClearWave telemetry, and audit/logging commitments.
2) Product will implement a per-customer telemetry opt-out flag and a routing rule to prevent forwarding to SummitMetrics for specific accounts; they will also produce a list of "required events" we cannot turn off for safety. Estimate: ~2–3 sprints for the engineering work.
3) Legal (Ben/Laura) — please find attached a draft subprocessor addendum we will propose; Ben, can you push the addendum + the redline into DocuSign once you and Laura are comfortable? We need a signed agreement before we begin forwarding any pilot telemetry.

Proposed customer-facing path: we can provisionally accept the pilot exception with the following conditions to be accepted in writing by ClearWave and SummitMetrics: (a) SummitMetrics SOC2 report uploaded to Redwood; (b) signed subprocessor addendum executed via DocuSign; (c) ClearWave agrees to the list of required events that will remain enabled. If those are satisfied, we can target begin date of Nov 22 for the pilot (gives 2 business weeks to collect evidence and sign).

Claire: are you able to coordinate SummitMetrics providing SOC2 and sign the addendum quickly? I’ll loop Ben to get DocuSign started once we have the green light.

Attachments: exceptions-matrix.xlsx (xls, 12KB) — internal mapping of risk vs mitigation.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
